# Reproducible-deployment constraints — the exact DIRECT dependency versions this project's
# test suite and validation battery were last verified against (Phase 7b.2, 2026-09-05).
#
# SCOPE (review P2 2026-09-03/2026-09-05). This file pins every DIRECT dependency across all
# extras — including pyomo, pre-commit and pip, previously unpinned. It is the INPUT to the
# deterministic lock, not the lock itself. The genuine byte-for-byte guarantee is `requirements.lock`:
#   * a RESOLVER-COMPLETE, HASH-PINNED lock of the FULL transitive closure, generated by
#     `scripts/gen_lock.py` (uv / pip-tools, `--generate-hashes --universal`) from this file +
#     pyproject.toml, with platform markers (e.g. watchdog on non-Darwin);
#   * GitHub Actions are pinned by commit SHA in .github/workflows/ci.yml;
#   * the CI `reproducible` job (a) fails if requirements.lock drifts from a fresh resolve
#     (`gen_lock.py --check`) and (b) PROVES a clean venv installs from the lock with
#     `pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.lock` followed by `pip check`.
# So "reproducible" is a TESTED deterministic lock installed end-to-end, not an ambient snapshot.
#
# For a reproducible install (consulting deployment, CI, reproducing a published result):
#
#     pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.lock      # byte-for-byte, hashes enforced
#     # or, to develop against the ranges with the direct pins applied:
#     pip install -e '.[data,cge,gui,dev]' -c constraints.txt
#
# Refresh BOTH this file and requirements.lock (`python scripts/gen_lock.py`) when re-verifying
# against a newer stack (bump the date above). pymrio in particular emits forward-compat (pandas)
# warnings across minor releases; pinning it keeps a deployment on a quiet, tested combination.

# --- resolver ---
pip==24.3.1

# --- core ---
pydantic==2.11.9
pandas==2.3.3
pyyaml==6.0.3
numpy==2.3.3

# --- data extra ([data]) ---
pymrio==0.6.3
duckdb==1.5.5
pyarrow==24.0.0

# --- cge extra ([cge]) ---
# pyomo is used by the optional Pyomo-backed solver path AND installed by the CI reproducible job
# (the [cge] extra), so it must be pinned here (review P2 2026-09-03: previously commented out).
pyomo==6.9.4
scipy==1.16.2

# --- gui extra ([gui]) ---
streamlit==1.61.1
altair==6.2.2

# --- dev extra ([dev]) ---
# Pinned so the constrained CI job (ci.yml `reproducible` job) runs a byte-stable toolchain.
# pre-commit is installed by the [dev] extra and was previously unpinned (review P2 2026-09-03).
pytest==8.4.2
ruff==0.16.0
pre-commit==4.4.0
